title: Barcelona Player Ratings vs. Atletico Madrid: Fermin Magic Keeps Barca at La Liga Summit
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellNov 8, 2026Fermín Lopez led Barcelona to victory. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesBarcelona came from behind to secure a gritty 2–1 win over Atlético Madrid on Sunday, keeping their place atop the La Liga standings ahead of the November international break.

The Catalans were second best in the early stages at the Metropolitano, completely on the back foot as Diego Simeone’s men ran wild. It felt like a goal was coming from the hosts and it took them just 10 minutes to get the better of Barcelona’s high line.

Julián Alvarez, who should have scored just a few minutes prior, set up Giuliano Simeone to give Atlético Madrid the early lead. They kept the pressure on, but the defending Spanish champions kept their nerve and waited for their moment to strike.

Fermín Lopez bagged an equalizer in the 45th minute, sending a first-time strike past Jan Oblak to bring the score level. There was a bit of good fortune for the ball to ricochet right to the Spain international, but his finish was as classy as they come.
Barcelona took full control of the game in the second half and it was Fermín again, with another first-time hit, to give Hansi Flick’s side the 2–1 lead in the 66th minute.
It was all business from the Catalans as the minutes ticked on. Atlético Madrid never looked truly capable of salvaging a result, and Barça were the deserved winners once the final whistle sounded.

Fermín Lopez put Barcelona on his back. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesNearly every headline about Barcelona’s strong start to 2026–27 has centered around the dazzling Lamine Yamal or the unstoppable Raphinha. Constantly overlooked was Fermín—until Sunday.

The No. 10 was the difference in a tightly contested match between two of the best teams in Spain. When the Catalans looked like they had no grasp on the game in the first half, it was Fermín who wrapped his foot around the ball to give the visitors a lifeline on the brink of halftime.

When the Catalans looked like they had no answers against Atlético Madrid’s disciplined defense in the second half, it was Fermín who beat Oblak again, putting the team on his back and bailing out the underwhelming forwards playing in front of him.

Anthony Gordon showed little signs of life, Raphinha might as well have not been on the pitch and Yamal was swarmed every time he touched the ball. Barcelona needed a hero to emerge if they were going to win the game and Fermín answered the call.
The Spain international now has 15 goal contributions in 16 appearances this season, making his case as one of the best attacking midfielders in Europe.
Barcelona kept the top spot in La Liga. / David Ramos/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Joan García—7.4: Under pressure from the opening whistle and weathered the storm with poise, keeping his team in the game. Almost caught off his line in the second half, but Alvarez put too much power on his chip attempt.
RB: Brian Fariñas—6.2: Showed his inexperience going up against the lethal Julián Alvarez. Looked completely out of his depth against the Argentine in transition. Hooked at halftime.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—7.6: Stablized as the game progressed. Hardly put a foot wrong with the ball at his feet and adapted well to playing alongside Christensen in the second half.
CB: Gerard Martín—7.6: Inexplicably didn’t even try tracking Simeone’s run into the box. Moved to left back in the second half and did well playing at his old position.

LB: João Cancelo—6.5: Caught in no man’s land on Atlético Madrid’s opening goal. His night never got better, putting together a performance littered with careless mistakes. Deservedly replaced at the hour-mark.
CM: Marc Bernal—7.6: Filled in admirably for the injured Rodri. Covered for his floundering backline in the first half and allowed Pedri to operate with complete freedom.

CM: Pedri—7.8: Showed off his silky passing in another game he effortlessly controlled. Knew when to push forward, when to slow down the tempo and when to pull the strings of the attack, like he did in the build-up to Fermín’s first goal.
